problem: Neural rough differential equations capture irregular sampling efficiently but cannot model Itô dynamics or manifold-constrained systems that require quadratic-variation terms and covariant derivatives.
approach: Branched Neural Rough Differential Equations (B-NRDEs) use a Hopf-algebraic framework matching governing calculus (Grossman-Larson trees for Euclidean Itô dynamics, Munthe-Kaas-Wright trees for manifolds) to recasts log-ODE steps as geometric numerical integration that preserves manifold constraints.
contribution: B-NRDEs unify stochastic and manifold-valued dynamics beyond the Euclidean-Stratonovich setting, demonstrated on rough Bergomi volatility, SO(3) forecasting, and SPD covariance dynamics.

problem: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning policies are vulnerable to action hijacking with limited compromised timesteps, and existing adversarial attacks fail to expose coordination weaknesses efficiently under attack budgets.
approach: Budgeted Hierarchical Efficient Attack (BHEA) separates when/which agents to hijack from action replacement, enabling precise vulnerability discovery under limited opportunities, combined with adversarial training to improve robustness.
contribution: BHEA demonstrates stronger attacks under the same budget and substantially improves robustness to limited-step action hijacking on StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC) while reducing training overhead.

problem: Self-speculative decoding in LLMs uses static heuristics that ignore dynamic computational overhead of attention in long-context scenarios, limiting throughput improvements.
approach: KnapSpec reformulates draft model selection as a knapsack problem maximizing tokens-per-time throughput by decoupling attention and MLP layers, modeling hardware-specific latencies as functions of context length via parallel dynamic programming.
contribution: KnapSpec achieves up to 1.47x wall-clock speedup on Qwen3 and Llama3 without training or output distribution changes, with rigorous theoretical analysis establishing cosine similarity as proxy for token acceptance.

problem: Neural Combinatorial Optimization methods for NP-hard routing and packing rely on task-specific augmentations, perform poorly on out-of-distribution instances, and lack robust inference mechanisms.
approach: LGS-Net proposes an instance-conditioned latent space model with Latent Guided Sampling (LGS), a Markov Chain Monte Carlo and Stochastic Approximation-based inference method with rigorous convergence guarantees.
contribution: LGS achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark routing tasks among neural combinatorial optimization baselines with theoretical convergence guarantees.

problem: Structure-preserving dynamics models require per-configuration training with explicit system parameters, limiting generalization when parameters vary and preventing few-shot adaptation.
approach: Integrating modulation-based meta-learning techniques into Hamiltonian learning frameworks enables parameter-agnostic few-shot adaptation that preserves conservation laws without explicit system parameterization.
contribution: Modulation-based meta-learning achieves accurate few-shot adaptation across parameter space while maintaining conservation of key invariants on benchmark problems.

problem: Meta-learning methods perform well on within-distribution tasks but fail on out-of-distribution targets where source task transfer can induce negative transfer.
approach: Condition task-specific priors on precomputed latent causal task embeddings in a Bayesian meta-learning framework, enabling transfer based on mechanistic similarity, with noisy expert pairwise judgments of causal similarity instead of target-task data.
contribution: Reduces negative transfer and improves out-of-distribution adaptation in simulations and clinical prediction for cross-disease transfer, with theoretical analysis showing conditioning on causal embeddings controls prior mismatch.

problem: Capturing and profiling minute wear particles in jet engines at high speeds is extremely difficult due to extreme background noise and low resolution in harsh environments.
approach: QuantWear uses quantum sensing to monitor Sodium and Potassium atomic spectral signatures that adhere to particle surfaces, leveraging quantum jump and Faraday rotation to suppress flame noise, then applies deep learning for quantification and 3D reconstruction from 2D images.
contribution: Achieves 22.5 dB imaging SNR and 95% 3D reconstruction similarity, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art wear particle detection technologies.

problem: Large language model training faces significant memory bottlenecks with memory-intensive optimizers like Adam, and existing memory-efficient approaches introduce computational overhead or degrade performance.
approach: FOAM compresses optimizer states via block-wise gradient means with residual correction, achieving convergence rates equivalent to vanilla Adam under non-convex settings while eliminating up to 90% of optimizer state memory.
contribution: FOAM eliminates up to 90% of optimizer state memory overhead, accelerates convergence, and integrates with other memory-efficient optimizers with performance matching or surpassing full-rank and existing baselines.

problem: Music reward model evaluation remains fragmented and narrowly focused despite music generation models handling complex multimodal inputs mixing text, lyrics, and reference audio.
approach: Establish CMI ecosystem with 110k pseudo-labeled preference samples (CMIPref-Pseudo) and high-quality human-annotated corpus (CMI-Pref), introducing CMI-RewardBench unified benchmark and parameter-efficient CMI reward models (CMI-RMs) for heterogeneous multimodal inputs.
contribution: CMI-RM correlates strongly with human judgments on Music Arena and CMI-Pref, enables effective inference-time scaling via topk filtering, advancing aligned music generation.

problem: Multi-agent LLM collaboration typically relies on centralized execution and predefined protocols, and Monte Carlo fine-tuning methods suffer from high variance in decentralized settings.
approach: Propose Multi-Agent Actor-Critic (MAAC) methods for decentralized LLM collaboration: CoLLM-CC with centralized critic and CoLLM-DC with decentralized critics to optimize parallel inference.
contribution: CoLLM-CC outperforms Monte Carlo and CoLLM-DC on long-horizon and sparse-reward tasks, demonstrating when centralized vs decentralized critics benefit decentralized LLM collaboration.

problem: Achieving proactive real-time interactive AI companions faces three challenges: low-latency streaming inference, autonomous response timing, and balancing quality and quantity under time constraints.
approach: Introduce Live Gaming Benchmark with commentary and guidance scenarios, and Proact-VL framework that shapes multimodal language models into proactive real-time agents via environment perception and autonomous interaction.
contribution: Proact-VL achieves superior response latency and quality while maintaining strong video understanding on gaming scenarios, demonstrating practicality for real-time interactive applications.

problem: LLM alignment relies on complex reward signals that obscure specific incentivized behaviors, creating risks of misalignment and reward hacking, with existing methods missing unknown unknowns.
approach: Obj-Disco automatically decomposes alignment reward signals into sparse weighted combinations of human-interpretable objectives via iterative greedy analysis across training checkpoints.
contribution: Obj-Disco captures >90% of reward behavior across diverse tasks and models, identifying latent misaligned incentives alongside intended behaviors, enabling more transparent alignment.

problem: Active mapping struggles to achieve zero-shot generalization to large-scale scenes and lacks language instruction support for embodied agents.
approach: Introduce 360-BEV representation integrating omnidirectional semantics with geometric structure, develop VLM-based waypoint generation in image space back-projected to 3D actions, and design depth-first exploration organizing scenes into topological trees.
contribution: Without task-specific training, improves coverage and AUC by 13.25% and 14.00% over strongest baseline while enabling language-conditioned interaction.

problem: Nearest neighbor search requires trading off accuracy of expensive ground-truth metrics against efficiency of cheap proxy metrics.
approach: Bi-metric framework constructs data structures using only cheap proxy metrics but achieves accuracy of expensive ground-truth metrics through limited queries to both metrics during search.
contribution: Achieves arbitrarily good approximation guarantees with bounded-factor proxy metrics on DiskANN and Cover Tree, substantially improving accuracy-efficiency tradeoff on BEIR text retrieval benchmark.

problem: Language models suffer from distribution shifts where observable and unobservable components combine, causing omitted variable bias that compromises both evaluation and optimization.
approach: Framework separates distribution shifts into observable and unobservable components, mapping omitted variable strength to worst-case generalization bounds for out-of-distribution performance.
contribution: Provides more principled out-of-distribution performance measures and improves true performance relative to standard methods, enabling inference about omitted variable strength.

problem: Multimodal LLMs suffer from object hallucination, where they generate descriptions of objects not present in images.
approach: Instruction Lens Score (InsLen) analyzes instruction token embeddings that implicitly encode visual information, combining Calibrated Local Score with Context Consistency Score for hallucination detection.
contribution: InsLen serves as a plug-and-play hallucination detector without auxiliary models or training, consistently outperforming existing methods across benchmarks and MLLM architectures.

problem: LLMs deployed on complex multi-step tasks may lack adequate algorithmic reasoning abilities, but lack diagnostic benchmarks specifically evaluating structural reasoning.
approach: DSR-Bench uses data structures as principled lens for probing structural reasoning across 20 structures, 35 operations, and 4,140 instances with hierarchical organization and automated evaluation.
contribution: Benchmarking 13 state-of-the-art LLMs reveals critical limitations with top model achieving only 0.46/1 on challenging instances, exposing poor spatial reasoning and code-based reasoning.

problem: Spectral graph neural networks based on graph Fourier transform are rarely used in GNNs due to expensive eigendecomposition and lack of vertex-domain locality, limiting ability to model long-range dependencies.
approach: L2G-Net factors the GFT into subgraph operators combined via Cauchy matrices, enabling exact spectral representations without full eigendecompositions by exploiting graph topology.
contribution: Scales to large graphs with long-range dependencies, competitive with state-of-the-art methods using orders of magnitude fewer learnable parameters.

problem: Hallucination evaluation benchmarks remain fragmented and English-centric, lacking structured factual resources like knowledge graphs despite their utility for hallucination mitigation.
approach: MultiHal bridges KG and multilinguality gaps with a KG-based multilingual benchmark mining 140k KG-paths, curated to 25.9k high-quality samples, with KG-RAG integration.
contribution: Shows 0.12-0.36 point improvement in semantic similarity, 0.16-0.36 in NLI entailment, and 0.29-0.42 in hallucination detection with KG-RAG over vanilla QA across languages.

problem: Fixed-geometry latent models cannot simultaneously model flexible peptide sequences with conformational diversity and physical feasibility due to coupled sequence-structure relationships.
approach: PepFGLD combines FlexEGNN for flexibility-aware geometric representations, bidirectional sequence-structure interaction through latent mappings, and time-dependent energy-guided diffusion to guide sampling toward physically feasible structures.
contribution: Improves binding affinity and design success across peptide design tasks by better handling interfacial flexibility and maintaining physical feasibility.

problem: Latent chain-of-thought methods use internal latent steps but intermediate computations are difficult to evaluate beyond correlation-based probes.
approach: Model latent steps as variables in structural causal models and analyze effects through step-wise do-interventions to identify causally necessary steps, influence propagation, and competing answer modes.
contribution: Reveals latent-step budgets behave as staged functionality with non-local routing, persistent gap between early output bias and late representational commitment, motivating mode-conditional training.

problem: Fairness in sequential decision-making needs principled quantification of counterfactual direct, indirect, and spurious effects in online learning with unknown fairness constraints.
approach: Formulate online causally-fair learning with multiple long-term constraints using counterfactual fairness measures in both contextual bandits and logistic bandits settings.
contribution: Achieves sublinear regret and violation bounds without Slater's condition, with O(1) per-round complexity for logistic bandits using online mirror descent.

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is overparameterized with multiple low-rank factor pairs yielding identical adapted weights but different condition numbers, impacting convergence rates.
approach: Balanced LoRA (BaLoRA) projects iterates onto a balanced manifold that improves loss landscape conditioning while preserving adapted matrices, integrating as a lightweight step into fine-tuning pipelines.
contribution: BaLoRA converges faster than standard LoRA and achieves superior performance across fine-tuning tasks.

problem: Remote sensing data distributed across institutions presents challenges for centralized processing due to communication costs and privacy concerns, complicating multi-view clustering.
approach: Deep federated multi-view clustering framework shares only privatized prototypes masked with adaptive noise, employs superpixel segmentation for dimensionality reduction, and uses Wasserstein prototype contrastive learning.
contribution: Achieves superior clustering performance and efficiency with communication efficiency and privacy preservation on remote sensing benchmarks.

problem: Standard leaderboard aggregation via Bradley-Terry models produces single global rankings incompatible with heterogeneous user preferences across diverse tasks.
approach: Pluralistic leaderboards adapted from social choice theory maintain stability with respect to heterogeneous populations via local stability guarantees while requiring only O~(k) pairwise comparisons.
contribution: Shows standard Bradley-Terry violates local stability in LMArena data, with proposed method providing substantially stronger stability guarantees.

problem: Bio-foundation models achieve strong performance but their robustness to biologically plausible perturbations and ML transformations remains underexplored, risking deployment failures.
approach: Systematically probe 11 state-of-the-art bio-FMs with 2,128 experiments on perturbation suites mimicking biological corruptions and ML preprocessing choices.
contribution: Reveals most bio-FMs are vulnerable to biological perturbations and ML transformations despite strong baseline performance, with cryo-EM models showing surprising robustness.

problem: Generating supervision for code repair at scale requires leveraging unit tests as verifiers, but self-play can drift from real-world bugs despite improving repair on synthetic bugs.
approach: Anchored Self-Play (ASP) uses code-embedding similarity reward and mixes reference bugs into training to anchor self-play, with new BugSourceBench spanning human/LM/edited-LM bugs.
contribution: ASP improves average fix rate by 25% relative / 7.2pp absolute over standard self-play, with gains on both LM-error bugs (+100% relative) and human-authored bugs (+7.1% relative).

problem: Autoregressive LLMs fail at simple logical reasoning like the reversal curse where trained on forward knowledge A→B but unable to deduce reversal B→A.
approach: Simple regularization data recipe called Identity Bridge adding A→A examples during training tweaks the optimization landscape to enable reversal reasoning.
contribution: Under Identity Bridge recipe, 1B model achieves 50% success on reversal tasks vs near-zero baseline, with theoretical proof that one-layer transformer breaks reversal curse under implicit bias.

problem: Generalization in overparameterized deep neural networks is poorly understood from parameter-centric analyses.
approach: Derive post-hoc generalization bounds relating population-empirical risk gap to embedding intrinsic dimension and downstream mapping sensitivity via Lipschitz constants.
contribution: Embedding dimension dominates generalization at final layer, providing post-hoc explanation and enabling embedding-based diagnostics for trained models.

problem: Selective State Space Models like Mamba have linear complexity but transform systems from linear time-invariant to linear parameter-varying, where individually stable matrices can produce unbounded trajectories under switching.
approach: Control-theoretic framework analyzes selective SSMs as continuous-time LTI sampling, establishing BIBO stability, two-term robustness bounds, and algorithms to extract certificate constants from trained weights.
contribution: First comprehensive stability and robustness analysis of selective SSMs with formal guarantees enabling certification for safety-critical deployment.

problem: Step-level diffusion caching uses threshold-based heuristics for per-step decisions without directly optimizing final output quality, making inference latency uncontrollable.
approach: BudCache inverts formulation to fix compute budget and search for cache policy best preserving output via Simulated Annealing with Hill Climbing, with cache-aware schedule alignment.
contribution: On FLUX.1-dev and Wan2.1, achieves better generation quality than heuristic baselines under tight compute budgets.

problem: Relationship between model performance and unembedding matrix geometry, particularly effective rank, remains unclear for downstream task prediction.
approach: Systematic investigation of 108 OLMo-style models trained under controlled variation, analyzing relationship between effective rank and performance across tasks.
contribution: High effective rank correlates with best performance but trend is not universal; effective rank primarily reflects training choices like batch size and weight decay rather than performance.

problem: Flow Matching models enable high-quality generation but rely on expensive ODE-based iterative sampling, and existing distillation approaches fail to exploit geometric structure.
approach: Mean Flow Distillation (MFD) acts as temporal low-pass filter suppressing high-frequency optimization noise while ensuring trajectory consistency, with Mean Flow Matching Theorem.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on high-dimensional manifolds including 4D occupancy forecasting and text-to-image generation, enabling high-fidelity single-step generation.

problem: Millimeter-wave sensing produces sparse, temporally irregular, noisy measurements, and existing ANN pipelines require extensive preprocessing or deep architectures limiting edge deployment.
approach: Study SNNs via mechanism-data alignment perspective leveraging leaky integrate-and-fire low-pass filtering behavior, deriving frequency-matching criterion for membrane decay configuration.
contribution: 6.22% test-accuracy improvement and 3.64x energy reduction vs ANN baselines on mmWave datasets when frequency-matching LIF bandwidth to data's discriminative spectrum.

problem: Federated fine-tuning faces severe client resource heterogeneity where existing truncation-based methods couple transmitted and trainable ranks, under-utilizing communication-rich compute-limited clients.
approach: FedHera decouples information reception from optimization with spectrum-preserving rank allocation maximizing global knowledge transfer within bandwidth limits, plus prefix-gating mechanism using frozen basis as reference.
contribution: Improves stability and accuracy over baselines under heterogeneous resource settings while reducing truncation-induced gradient drift.

problem: Extracting implicit safety objectives from crowd preference datasets is challenging, but preferences may embed shared safety principles transferable to downstream tasks.
approach: Hierarchical framework extracts safety-aligned skills from crowd preferences using Safe Crowd Preference-based RL that composes skills via high-level policy.
contribution: Substantially lowers safety costs without access to explicit safety rewards while achieving task performance comparable to oracle methods with ground-truth signals.

problem: Certified robustness against poisoning in graph neural networks remains underexplored, and partitioning-aggregation methods fail under sparse label and structure conditions.
approach: Deep Self-Training Graph Partition Aggregation (ST-GPA) enriches graph partitions with pseudo-labels and synthetic edges enabling effective certification under sparsity.
contribution: Architecture-agnostic framework significantly improves robustness guarantees against node-label and graph-structure poisoning while maintaining clean accuracy on benchmarks.

problem: LLM agentic workflows involve multiple LLM and tool requests but existing systems schedule and allocate resources per-request without end-to-end workflow knowledge, causing suboptimal KV cache management.
approach: ThunderAgent abstracts agentic workflows as LLM Programs enabling unified view of resources including KV caches and tool environments, with program-aware scheduler and tool resource manager.
contribution: Achieves 1.5-3.6x throughput improvements in serving, 1.8-3.9x in RL rollout, and up to 4.2x disk memory savings over state-of-the-art systems.

problem: Domain generalization via flat minima is limited by two challenges: uniform optimization ignoring domain-specific difficulty and anisotropic sharpness along single gradient directions.
approach: Dual Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization (DA-SAM) combines Dynamic Adaptive Scaling for domain-specific perturbations and Adaptive Multi-Directional Flattening for multi-directional geometric exploration.
contribution: DA-SAM guides model parameters away from anisotropic sharp regions with domain-level guidance, improving domain generalization robustness.

problem: LLM monitors detect misbehavior but contemporary systems often perform better with less information, the less-is-more effect, making information filtering critical.
approach: Extract-and-Evaluate (EaE) monitoring uses hierarchical approach where one monitor isolates relevant excerpts from trajectories and another scores excerpts, filtering information for detection.
contribution: In BigCodeBench-Sabotage with GPT-4.1-mini, EaE improves sabotage detection by 16.8 percentage points over next-best baseline with linear cost scaling.
